summary: Explains and describes the reassignment of well-known ports for the One-Way Active Measurement Protocol (OWAMP) and the Two-Way Active Measurement Protocol (TWAMP) control and measurement traffic. It updates RFC 4656 and RFC 5357 for UDP port assignments and clarifies the protocol names. It is a standards-track document.

eli5.summary: Network measurement tools need agreed meeting spots so they can find each other. This document sorts out which door numbers those tools should use.

questions: which udp port does twamp test use
subtitle: Moves the well-known UDP ports 861 and 862 from the OWAMP and TWAMP control protocols to their test protocols.

tldr.problem: The control protocols of OWAMP and TWAMP use TCP, yet UDP well-known ports had been assigned to them, while the UDP test protocols had no well-known port.
tldr.mechanism: IANA reassigned UDP port 861 to OWAMP-Test and UDP port 862 to TWAMP-Test, leaving the TCP assignments as they were. Use of the port is OPTIONAL.
tldr.outcome: Implementations may use a well-known default port for test traffic, and a Control-Client can request it while a Server can offer an alternate port. The memo also clarifies that both control and test protocols are required for OWAMP and TWAMP.

today: RFC 8545 is a Proposed Standard from March 2019 that updates RFC 4656 and RFC 5357. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Two Protocols, Two Parts Each
sections.content:
The IETF IP Performance Metrics (IPPM) Working Group developed the One-Way Active Measurement Protocol (OWAMP) in RFC 4656, and later the Two-Way Active Measurement Protocol (TWAMP) in RFC 5357.

Each needs a control and mode negotiation protocol (OWAMP-Control and TWAMP-Control) that uses TCP, including security configuration and key derivation. The control protocols set up and manage test sessions that use the matching test protocol (OWAMP-Test or TWAMP-Test) over UDP. The IETF saw value in assigning a well-known UDP port to the test protocols, and noted that this can be done by reassigning ports.
sections.eli5: One part of the tool talks to plan the test, and the other part sends the test messages. This document is about giving the second part a standard address.

sections.title: What OWAMP and TWAMP Consist Of
sections.content:
The memo clarifies naming. OWAMP-Control is defined in Section 3 of RFC 4656 and OWAMP-Test in Section 4. TWAMP-Control and TWAMP-Test are in Sections 3 and 4 of RFC 5357. Implementing both parts is REQUIRED for Standards Track OWAMP and TWAMP.

TWAMP Light is an idea from Appendix I of RFC 5357: an unspecified control protocol combined with TWAMP-Test. It was placed in an appendix because it had no specification for negotiating this form of operation and none for mandatory-to-implement security. Appendix A of RFC 8545 gives the background, citing an Area Director review and a ballot discuss. Since TWAMP Light includes TWAMP-Test, the memo considers it reasonable for future systems to use the TWAMP-Test well-known UDP port.
sections.eli5: A full tool needs both the planning part and the testing part. A cut-down version that skips the planning part is only an idea, not a finished standard.

sections.title: The Reassigned Ports
sections.content:
Originally both TCP and UDP well-known ports had been assigned to the control protocols. Because OWAMP-Control and TWAMP-Control need TCP, they cannot use the UDP ports. IANA therefore moved the UDP well-known port from the control protocol to the test protocol. Using this port is OPTIONAL in Standards Track OWAMP and TWAMP.

The memo says a well-known port may simplify operations and can serve as a default for future specifications involving TWAMP-Test. It names the Broadband Forum's TR-390, a specification for testing at the customer edge of IP networks, as an example that benefits.
sections.eli5: The planning door only works with one kind of connection, so it never used its second number. That spare number now belongs to the test door.

sections.title: Negotiating the Receiver Port
sections.content:
In TWAMP, the Control-Client proposes a Receiver Port, normally from the Dynamic Ports range in RFC 6335. If that port is unavailable, the Server at the Session-Reflector MAY suggest an alternate port in the Port field. Otherwise the Server uses the Accept field to signal rejection and MUST NOT suggest an alternate port, setting the Port field to zero. This text updates Section 3.5 of RFC 5357 per Erratum ID 1587.

A Control-Client that supports the allocated port MAY request it in the Request-TW-Session command. A Server that does not support it replies with an alternate port in the Accept-Session message with Accept field = 0, so the change is backward compatible. OWAMP works the same way using the Request-Session command.

For equal-cost multipath testing, varying only one element of the five-tuple, such as the source port, is enough to monitor different paths. Using the reallocated port is optional, so it has no negative impact on this.
sections.eli5: A client can ask to use the standard test door. If the other side cannot use it, it names a different door, so old software keeps working.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The considerations for any active measurement of live paths apply, as described in RFC 4656 and RFC 5357. Active techniques reveal much less sensitive information to observers than passive observation of user traffic, whose privacy issues are covered in the LMAP framework (RFC 7594).

The registered UDP port could become a target of denial of service or aid man-in-the-middle attacks. To protect against denial of service, the memo recommends filtering access to the Receiver Port with an access list and using a non-globally routable address for the Session-Reflector. Authenticated mode lets an implementation detect modified test packets, and encrypted mode also prevents eavesdropping. A network under test might also give special treatment to flows using the well-known port and so bias results.
sections.eli5: A famous door is easier for troublemakers to find, so guard it, and use sealed envelopes so nobody can change the test results. Also, a network could cheat by treating test traffic nicely.

sections.title: The IANA Port Table
sections.content:
IANA reallocated two UDP ports from the System Ports range of the Service Name and Transport Protocol Port Number Registry: 861 and 862. The TCP assignments were left as they were. IANA also changed the Assignee and Contact for these ports, both UDP and TCP, to the IESG and the IETF Chair.

  • owamp-test, port 861, udp, OWAMP-Test Receiver Port, RFC 8545
  • twamp-control, port 862, tcp, TWAMP-Control, RFC 5357
  • twamp-test, port 862, udp, TWAMP-Test Receiver Port, RFC 8545
sections.eli5: Door 861 and door 862 each have a talking side and a testing side, now listed clearly in the official address book.
